featured_reviews.name: Sushmita Mohite
featured_reviews.review_text:
Panshikar had been on my list for its reputation for Maharashtrian snacks, and I finally visited yesterday evening. Conveniently located just outside Dadar railway station, I was eager to try their specialties.
I started with the Misal Pav, which wasn't quite my style due to the farsan, poha, and batatyachi bhaji making it a bit soggy. However, the taste was decent, though slightly on the sweeter side.
Next, I tried the Bhajani Thalipeet it was deep-fried and tasted good, paired with their lasun chutney, which was absolutely delicious.
The star of the evening, however, was the Kothimbir Vadi. It was perfectly cooked—crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, making it an absolute treat.
I ended the meal with Piyush which is a must-try and a great way to conclude the meal.
Overall, the experience was good. The service was fast and efficient, and I appreciated the quick turnaround. A heads-up: Panshikar is closed on Sundays.
If you're in the mood for some classic Maharashtrian snacks, this is definitely worth a visit!

featured_reviews.name: Vigyan Anand
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a traveler constantly on the hunt for authentic local food experiences, finding Ghasitaram's online store was a fantastic discovery! I usually prefer street food, but when I needed a reliable source for high-quality, traditional Indian sweets and farsan (savory snacks) to take home as gifts and for myself, their website was a lifesaver.
The sheer variety of their offerings is incredible—from classic Besan Laddoos and rich Kaju Katli to various types of crunchy Namkeens. It felt like walking into a massive, traditional Indian sweet shop without leaving my hotel room! The best part? The "Traditional Sweets & Farsan" claim is absolutely genuine. The Gulab Jamuns were soft and soaked in a perfectly balanced syrup, and the Bombay Mix had that quintessential, fresh crunch that tells you it's made with care. It truly captures the taste of an old-world halwai (sweet maker).
The online ordering experience was clean and straightforward, which is exactly what a traveler needs when dealing with unfamiliar websites. My order was packed securely and delivered right to my temporary accommodation in a timely manner. The beautiful, quality packaging made them ideal for gifting, too. If you’re a tourist looking to bring back a genuine taste of Indian tradition, skip the generic souvenir shops and order from Ghasitaram. Highly, highly recommended for a delicious and authentic culinary souvenir!

name: Joshi Budhakaka Mahim Halwawala
description:
Set-up in the pre-Independence era, Joshi Budhakaka Mahim Halvawala is the oldest mithai and farsan establishment in India.

We have been serving Indians and Indians across the globe for over two centuries.
The fascinating journey goes back to 1780s when Joshi Jethabhai along with his main Mavji and Girdhar began their journey in the foot from Gujarat's Jaam Khambhaliya town to eventually settle down in Mahim, Mumbai.

Initially, selling Ghatiya door-to-door, Joshi Dhanji Girdhar pioneered the Mahim Halva (also referred as Ice and Paper halva) around 1830.

Over the years,the legacy of Mahim Halva has grown manifold to truly become an 'iconic' Indian sweets.

I recently ordered from Purshottamm Kandoi Haribhai Damodar Mithaiwala (what a legendary name for a legendary place!) to celebrate the fantastic victory of Mrs. Sheetal Gambhir in the recent BMC elections. As a proud supporter, I wanted something special, authentic, and indulgent to mark the occasion, and this iconic Mumbai sweet shop (since 1952!) delivered beyond expectations. I gave it a perfect 5-star rating on the app, and here’s why it truly deserves every bit of it.
The order included:
•	Vati Dhokla (those fluffy, perfectly steamed yellow cubes with the classic tempering of mustard seeds, curry leaves, and green chilies – soft, spongy, and bursting with tangy flavor)
•	Kothimbir Wadi (fresh, herby coriander-packed slices that were crispy outside and moist inside – a Gujarati classic done to perfection)
•	Healthy Cutlets (surprisingly delicious, packed with nuts and veggies, great texture, and a guilt-free snack option)
•	And the absolute star of the show – Kesar Rasmalai (12 pieces)!
Oh, the Kesar Rasmalai was pure bliss! The spongy chenna balls were soaked just right in thick, creamy, saffron-infused milk – not overly sweet, beautifully aromatic with real kesar strands, and topped with nuts for that premium touch. Each bite melted in the mouth, and the subtle cardamom flavor made it feel luxurious yet comforting. It was hands-down the best rasmalai I’ve had in a long time – fresh, rich, and so delicately balanced.
We enjoyed this delightful spread together at Smartflex Gym (shoutout to the amazing vibe there in Dadar West!), turning our post-workout session into a mini celebration feast. Sharing these treats with friends after a good sweat felt extra rewarding – the savory snacks fueled us perfectly, and the rasmalai was the ultimate sweet victory reward. Everything arrived fresh, well-packaged, and piping hot/cold as needed.
Purshottamm never disappoints with their authentic Gujarati flavors and consistent quality. This order was a complete winner – tasty, hygienic, timely delivery, and full of joy. Highly recommended for any celebration (or just because!). If you’re in Mumbai and craving genuine mithai and farsan, this is the place.
Thank you, Purshottamm, for making our celebration even sweeter! 🏆🍯✨
5/5 stars – will order again and again!

Panshikar & Co., established in 1931, stands as a true symbol of Mumbai’s old-world Maharashtrian charm. The moment you step in, you’re greeted with a nostalgic warmth — simple décor, authentic aromas, and that unmistakable traditional touch that feels like home.

The menu brings forth classic Maharashtrian dishes — from fluffy thalipeeth and misal to melt-in-the-mouth modaks and sabudana vada, each dish reflects the purity and simplicity of traditional cooking. The flavors are rich, authentic, and prepared with the kind of care that only a legacy eatery can offer.

Yes, the prices are a bit on the higher side, especially compared to the regular local joints, but considering the heritage, quality, and authenticity they maintain, it’s worth every rupee.

Panshikar & Co. isn’t just about food — it’s an experience that connects you to the roots of Maharashtra, one bite at a time.
